comment: Provenance is currently defined by the Client, Health Facility and Health Workforce registries — that is, by which person, which place and which worker. Once AI-drafted clinical content can enter a record, a third dimension is required: whether an entry was machine-generated or machine-drafted, by which system and version, and which human clinician reviewed and attested it. Without this, a Lifelong Health Record silently mixes human-authored and machine-drafted content and no subsequent audit, liability determination, quality review or model evaluation can separate them. This cannot be retrofitted: if the record structure does not carry the distinction from the outset, the historical record is permanently ambiguous. Because it concerns the foundational shared data layer rather than any point-of-service application, it belongs in this architecture and not in procurement guidance.

public.text: Provenance is currently defined by the Client, Health Facility and Health Workforce registries — that is, by which person, which place and which worker. Once AI-drafted clinical content can enter a record, a third dimension is required: whether an entry was machine-generated or machine-drafted, by which system and version, and which human clinician reviewed and attested it. Without this, a Lifelong Health Record silently mixes human-authored and machine-drafted content and no subsequent audit, liability determination, quality review or model evaluation can separate them. This cannot be retrofitted: if the record structure does not carry the distinction from the outset, the historical record is permanently ambiguous. Because it concerns the foundational shared data layer rather than any point-of-service application, it belongs in this architecture and not in procurement guidance.
public.suggestedRevision: Add to the provenance row of Table 2.2, and to the Lifelong Health Record component description, a requirement that record entries carry machine-generated content indicators: the authoring system and version, whether the content was machine-drafted, and the identity of the human clinician who reviewed and attested it. HL7 FHIR Provenance already supports the necessary structure, so this is a conformance expectation rather than a new component.
